key_insight: EgoReasoner enables robust egocentric 4D reasoning by learning task-adaptive structured thinking that continuously re-evaluates spatial relations under camera motion and object displacement.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of reasoning about objects and interactions in egocentric videos where both the camera and scene elements move, requiring continuous, viewpoint-relative spatio-temporal inference across time.
method: Task-adaptive structured thinking: decompose reasoning into specialized subroutines (spatial, temporal, viewpoint-aware) that are activated per task.
Egocentric 4D representations + memory: maintain trajectory-aware, camera-relative object representations to track movements, count interactions, and localize fixtures over time.

Unified benchmark and task-specific adapters: train and evaluate on a suite of tasks (fixture interaction counting, viewpoint-relative fixture location, movement itinerary tracking, stationary localization) with tailored losses or adapters for each task.
impact: Makes egocentric video understanding more reliable for downstream applications (robotics, AR, assistive tech) by providing modular, interpretable reasoning over time and changing viewpoints.
visual_elements: Timeline visualization showing camera motion + object trajectories (4D) with annotated events (interactions, stationary periods).

paper_title: EgoReasoner: Learning Egocentric 4D Reasoning via Task-Adaptive Structured Thinking
paper_authors: Fangrui Zhu, Yunfeng Xi, Jianmo Ni, Mu Cai, Boqing Gong
